correctness.rationale: Both graph definitions have 16 vertices, 48 edges, degree six and exactly two common neighbors per pair. The exact one-partner recurrence exhausts the matching families (2016 and 1920); the two alternative pairings of any two matching edges exhaust every legal four-cycle switch. The certificate records all 3936 states and 11328 undirected transitions. An independently structured C++ partner-array enumerator agrees on all components, radii, diameters, and eccentricity histograms; a separate certificate verifier reconstructs all states and all switches and runs complete all-source BFS. A direct proof also gives all 72 frozen rook matchings as three column four-cycles times 24 row assignments. No infinite conclusion is inferred from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Four-cycle switches are the minimal feasibility-preserving moves on perfect matchings and their connectivity controls whether the basic switch chain can explore the full matching space. The unique pair of nonisomorphic strongly regular graphs with parameters (16,6,2,2) isolates distinctions concealed by standard regularity data: 75 versus 13 components, 72 versus 12 frozen configurations, two 288-state subspaces in the rook graph and contrasting nontrivial diameters. The exact frozen rook family also has a natural four-cycle combinatorial description. These constitute a motivated finite structural classification; no broader family or mixing-time theorem is claimed.
